questions.prompt: Why is diamond transparent to most laser light?
choices: Single sub-bandgap photons can't be absorbed
questions.explain: The 5.5 eV gap is bigger than a visible/IR photon's energy.

questions.prompt: Diamond's extreme thermal conductivity means a hot spot…
choices: is cooled almost as fast as it's heated
questions.explain: The lattice conducts heat away very fast.

questions.prompt: In which case does 'infinite time' actually help cut the diamond?
questions.explain: An isolated stone slowly preheats until it cuts.

questions.prompt: Graphitization runs away because graphite is…
questions.explain: Black graphite absorbs more → hotter → more graphite.

questions.prompt: A heat-sunk diamond can be cut by a very weak beam if you just wait long enough.
questions.explain: Heat-sunk → steady state instantly; time doesn't help. You need ~40 W locally.

questions.prompt: Set it up so that infinite time DOES help (a weak beam that eventually cuts).
questions.explain: Use the Isolated boundary with a modest absorbed power (above the ~1 W surface-loss limit).

questions.prompt: Put the diamond in the regime where it stays safe and NEVER cuts.
questions.explain: Heat-sink it, or drop the power/absorption so the steady spot stays below T_g.
